source.title: Leveraging chaotic transients in the training of artificial neural networks
source.authors: Pedro Jim'enez-Gonz'alez; Miguel C. Soriano; Lucas Lacasa

record.file_problem: Full text supplied, including appendices; no apparent truncation.
record.tranche_reason: The paper measures training dynamics and test accuracy under large learning rates, but does not measure the training classification error or the effects named in V1–V6. Its CIFAR-10 result reports reaching a 30% target test accuracy, not training error.
record.gate_note: The paper reports learning-rate sweeps, Lyapunov exponents, and epochs to a target test accuracy. These do not establish whether training classification error reaches zero or near zero, whether large models avoid bad minima, or the effects named in V3–V6. No rows qualify for the listed versions. Reported CIFAR-10, MNIST, and other task results are therefore not extracted as rows for this claim.
record.test_reason: Appendix C directly measures the largest eigenvalue of the training-loss Hessian during full-batch gradient descent and compares it with 2/η. This tests the edge-of-stability component of V5 using its original method and measure. The record incorrectly excludes sharpness as irrelevant.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate but incomplete: the authors also report that late-training sharpness approaches 2/η at learning rates minimizing time to target test accuracy, and suggest that an early chaotic transient precedes this edge-of-stability behavior. Their exploration-exploitation explanation remains an interpretation of the observed association.
record.recipe_differences: Full-batch gradient descent with constant learning rates; the measured outcomes concern test accuracy and training-trajectory dynamics, not the claim’s training-error outcomes.
record.method_sensitivity: Learning rate changes whether trajectories show positive Lyapunov exponents and affects epochs to the target test accuracy. The reported qualitative pattern is also examined across task, activation, depth, regularization, and architecture.

fits_no_version.finding: Positive trajectory Lyapunov exponents and minimum epochs to target test accuracy coincide over an intermediate learning-rate range across several tasks and architectures.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Transient chaotic training dynamics can coincide with faster attainment of a target test accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: Adding a second hidden layer increases the minimum time to target test accuracy approximately twentyfold.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The tested two-hidden-layer MNIST MLP reaches its test-accuracy target more slowly than the shallow MLP.

record.problems: The main MNIST setup uses one shallow architecture and full-batch gradient descent without dropout; the authors identify stochastic or mini-batch training and learning-rate schedules as open problems. The CIFAR-10 MLP uses a 30% target test accuracy because MLPs typically have limited performance on that task. The paper does not report training classification error for the claim’s listed versions.
record.rows_left_out: No eligible rows for V1–V6: reported outcomes are trajectory Lyapunov measures, training time to test-accuracy targets, or sharpness, rather than the behaviors those versions name.

untested.parts: Near-zero training classification error, corrupted labels, and model-size or training-recipe effects.
Teacher-student spurious minima and the effect of extra student neurons.
Depth-related training error with batch normalization and identity shortcuts; very deep plain networks and Fixup.
Controlled initialization comparisons affecting training speed or trainable depth.

Squared-loss wide-network recovery relative to the initial linearized stability limit; an explicit initial loss rise paired with curvature reduction; progressive sharpening from below; sustained loss descent while sharpness hovers at the threshold; and divergence from initially subthreshold learning rates.
Batch-normalization and Fixup comparisons for training speed, stability, and learning-rate tolerance.

missing.what: Add V5-linked sharpness trajectories for η = 7.5 and 10: the authors report bounded late-training sharpness close to 2/η, approximately 0.267 and 0.2 respectively. The record's blanket exclusion of sharpness incorrectly omits direct evidence on V5.
missing.locator: Appendix C, pages 6–7; Figure 14, page 8; main-text discussion on page 4.

record.verdict_notes: There are no existing rows to repair. Figure 1 reports training-loss trajectories, so the record's characterization of all outcomes as unrelated to training loss is inaccurate. Those trajectories alone do not establish the initial-stability-limit or squared-loss conditions in V5.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error, random or corrupted labels, model size effects, and the effects of early stopping or regularization on that error.
Teacher-student two-layer ReLU local minima and the effect of student width relative to teacher width.
Training error across depth with and without identity shortcuts, and the Fixup and very-deep plain-network comparisons.
Initialization comparisons and their effects on training speed or trainable depth.
Training loss behavior around the stability limit, edge-of-stability sharpness dynamics, and divergence rates.
Batch-normalization comparisons for training speed or learning-rate tolerance, and the Fixup comparison.

relationships.condition: MNIST tanh MLP, full-batch gradient descent, constant η = 7.5 and 10; late-training sharpness stabilization.
relationships.reason: Appendix C and Figure 14 report stabilized sharpness closely matching 2/η, supporting V5's threshold-hovering component. This verdict rests on the text; the record contains no corresponding rows.
relationships.display_finding: Late-training sharpness stabilized closely around 2/η at constant learning rates 7.5 and 10.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
